name: Aleut

ancestors.notes: Descent per Glottolog classification of Aleut (aleu1260).

notes: Skeleton. Eskimo-Aleut (Aleut/Unangam) language of the Aleutian Islands written in the Bergsland practical Latin orthography (Bergsland 1994, 1997) — the dominant modern writing system for Aleut (a historical Cyrillic orthography, introduced by Russian Orthodox missionaries in the 19th century, is now a minority/heritage convention; Latin is the one used in current pedagogical and dictionary materials, so it is the one modelled here). Long vowels are doubled (aa ii uu); ng=[ŋ], d=[ð], g=[ɣ] with circumflexed x̂=[χ] and ĝ=[ʁ] for the uvular fricatives, and l̂=[ɬ] are mapped. The h-prefixed voiceless sonorants (hm hn hng hl hw hy) are mapped to voiceless counterparts. Predictable stress is left unencoded. IMPORTANT — gold-vs-orthography finding: the NorthEuraLex `ale` forms were checked against this spec and do NOT match the Bergsland practical spelling. The gold uses a combining-acute ⟨x́⟩ (not the circumflex ⟨x̂⟩ Bergsland's orthography writes), hyphenates a stem/suffix boundary as a literal citation-form artifact, and — most importantly — shows a systematic vowel-quality shift not attested in Aleut phonology under Bergsland's analysis (unstressed i→[e], u→[y]/[o], a→[ɛ]/[ɑ] depending on the word, doubled ⟨aa⟩→[ɛː] rather than [aː]). This is a narrow phonetic transcription of a specific recorded pronunciation (or a distinct source dialect's realization), not the practical orthography Aleut is written in; modelling it as if it were the spelling would misdescribe the language. This spec therefore keeps the real Bergsland Latin orthography and stays at `skeleton` rather than chasing the gold's PER with orthography-violating rules.
